summary: The repository has the needed OAuth primitives, but the proposal crosses several existing ownership boundaries: Jira’s Identity Vault sink, channel-scoped broker interfaces, agent-scoped toolkit hydration, and MCP’s user-bound storage. The highest risks are silent credential divergence during migration, incomplete principal propagation, and retiring enablement before all session hydration paths change.

suggestions.title: Make Jira persistence an explicit principal-aware store adapter
suggestions.rationale: `AbstractOAuth2Manager` writes the generic channel-keyed vault and Redis entries, while `JiraOAuthManager` writes Redis first and then synchronizes the Identity Vault through `CredentialSink`; the sink tests require different link-time and refresh-time IdentityStore operations. Converting Jira directly to the base class can silently create a competing credential owner. Define an injected store/override seam that preserves Identity Vault as the durable source of truth and makes link, refresh, read, and revoke behavior explicit.

suggestions.title: Resolve a typed principal once and retain channel identity separately
suggestions.rationale: `TelegramUserSession.user_id` returns the Navigator ID only after login and otherwise returns `tg:<telegram_id>`, while the Telegram Jira commands still pass the raw Telegram ID and the broker/resolver contracts remain `(channel, user_id)`. A `nav_user_id` copied into OAuth state is insufficient for tool calls, refreshes, disconnects, and legacy migration. Introduce an explicit resolved-principal object or protocol with fail-closed behavior for absent or ambiguous mappings, while retaining channel/chat identifiers solely for notification delivery.

suggestions.title: Specify migration semantics for every legacy credential path before cutover
suggestions.rationale: The generic manager has channel-based Redis, lock, and vault names; Jira has a separate channel-based Redis cache and lock; the vault helper also embeds channel in OAuth names. “Read-new-then-legacy” must define precedence, collision handling, rewrite success, refresh behavior, and deletion for each path. Add a bounded metric for unbound Telegram keys and keep legacy reads until the metric and rollback criteria are satisfied; do not make forced reconnect the only recovery for an ambiguous mapping.

suggestions.title: Treat FEAT-144 reversal as a session-hydration migration, not only an API change
suggestions.rationale: The service and UI currently create `user_agent_toolkits` enablement rows, and `UserObjectsHandler` still hydrates cold sessions exclusively from those rows. Removing `confirm_enable` or changing `IntegrationsService` without replacing this hydration path will make connected providers disappear from new sessions, while deleting the collection would orphan existing state. Add a compatibility phase or replace hydration with principal-level provider registration before retiring the old routes and data.

suggestions.title: Do not expose the entire OAuth registry through generic channel commands
suggestions.rationale: `OAuth2ProviderRegistry` contains MCP providers whose manager and toolkit factory are intentionally `None`, in addition to normal user-facing integrations. A generic `/connect <provider>` must filter to providers that support the channel and have an approved flow, enforce PBAC before generating state, and use server-owned scopes. Otherwise a registry entry can become an accidental Telegram command or an authorization bypass.

suggestions.title: Centralize needs-auth mapping and preserve the richer broker payload
suggestions.rationale: `ToolManager` currently maps only `AuthorizationRequired`, while `CredentialRequired` lacks `tool_name`, scopes, and device-code fields and AgentTalk separately catches only `AuthorizationRequired`. Catching the second exception in one location will still leave divergent web, AgentTalk, A2A, and device-code behavior. Add one surface-neutral mapper or response model that preserves `auth_kind`, `user_code`, `verification_uri`, `expires_in`, provider, and tool name, then adapt each surface from that model.

suggestions.title: Adapt JiraToolkit to the broker seam as a client-construction change
suggestions.rationale: Setting `credential_provider='jira'` alone is not sufficient: JiraToolkit currently resolves credentials in `_pre_execute`, requires a permission context, constructs a per-channel/user client, and the read interface deliberately avoids the toolkit resolver because of incompatible call signatures. The implementation must choose one owner for resolution, derive the principal-based cache key, inject the broker credential or token set into client construction, and preserve direct-call failure behavior.

suggestions.title: Keep provider behavior in manager subclasses until the migration stabilizes
suggestions.rationale: The existing registry is metadata plus a manager/toolkit factory, and the generic manager already exposes subclass hooks. A descriptor field containing a post-exchange hook name adds dynamic dispatch and makes provider-specific identity/account selection harder to validate. Keep Jira and O365 subclasses for this feature, move only immutable metadata into descriptors, and defer full descriptor-as-data until two or more nontrivial providers demonstrate the same hook contract.

suggestions.title: Make MCP credential resolution request-scoped, not merely config-scoped
suggestions.rationale: MCP configuration and token storage currently retain a user identifier, while `VaultMCPTokenStorage` is constructed for one user and `ReadonlyContext` supplies the user only at tool-call time. Removing the add-time identifier requires a per-call storage/token supplier or per-principal session factory; otherwise a shared MCP client can reuse one user’s token for another concurrent call. Add explicit fail-closed behavior when context has no user and concurrency tests with two principals.

suggestions.title: Define event ordering and delivery failure semantics before adding notifiers
suggestions.rationale: The current Jira flow writes Redis and treats Identity Vault sink failure as non-fatal, while the event fanout pattern is publish-only and `UserSocketManager` is process-local and username-keyed. If completion is published after Redis but before durable ownership, the UI and channel notifier can report a connection that is not recoverable; if notifier failure propagates, OAuth callbacks become unreliable. Emit an idempotent event only after the chosen source-of-truth write, make notifier delivery best-effort/retriable, and keep popup postMessage as a correctness path.

suggestions.title: Add a cross-channel migration matrix before deleting legacy routes
suggestions.rationale: Existing tests primarily cover channel-specific callback branches, sink behavior, and agent-scoped integration status. The new acceptance gate should test one principal connecting in Telegram and reading from web/Slack/Teams, unlinked Telegram forced reconnect, old-key migration and rollback, rotating refresh under concurrency, durable revoke, duplicate callbacks, missing principal state, both needs-auth exceptions, and two concurrent MCP users. These tests should use fake stores and deterministic Redis fixtures so provider availability is not part of correctness.
